intro.en: The doctor has given Hamo some advice, and Xezo has written it down. The neighbours keep bringing jars of honey, and Hevalo is guarding them. In the morning one jar is empty. Read the evidence on the board, answer each question, then say who ate the honey.

about.en: Xezo’s uncle, who is not feeling well.
The young deer, who was guarding the jars.

line.en: And advice number three: honey at night is forbidden!
But honey is forbidden. I’m taking the jars, and Hevalo is guarding them.
No, Baran is not at home today.
I’m innocent! I only like apples.
Forbidden? But honey makes me strong!
All right, all right… I’ll hide the honey under the bedding.
In the morning… What’s this? A jar is empty! Who is the thief?
Uncle… why is your moustache full of honey?
My moustache? I… I’m innocent too!

prompt.en: Why could Baran not have eaten the honey?
What does Hevalo say he likes?
What did Xezo see in the morning?

solution.en: The doctor forbade honey at night, and Xezo wrote it down. Hevalo was guarding the jars, but he only likes apples, and Baran was not at home. Hamo said honey makes him strong and spoke of hiding honey under the bedding — and in the morning his moustache was full of honey. Hamo ate the honey.

hints.en: Read what each suspect says, and find out who was not there at all.
One of the cards is what Xezo saw in the morning.
Which of the suspects has a moustache?
